kind: read-only source census (lifetime and synchronization inventory)
scope: This is source reading of the Fluent Bit checkout at the pinned revision only; it is not an audit verdict, not a Quirin result, not a model proof and not a native observation, and no entry in it (including every candidate label C*, N*, A*, BC-*, BX-*, S1) is an upstream defect finding.
method: Line ranges verified with nl -ba / sed -n / Read against the pinned checkout; sha256sum recorded per cited file. No git, build or execution. Prior investigations (docs/reports/fb-system-audit-cards/retry, docs/reports/fb-system-audit-cards/accounting) were re-checked at the pin rather than copied; their candidates appear under failure_outcomes.cross_references with re-verified lines.

selection.widening_rule: Headers and flb_output_thread.c / flb_input.c / flb_config.c are cited only where a lifetime decision or shutdown ordering lives there. Any other target is recorded as outside_selection with its path and is used only as a callee summary or definition site.

identities.name: ChunkIO chunk as used by Fluent Bit
identities.identity_key: pointer (struct cio_chunk *); no generation field; name string (ch->name) unique only within its stream. sb.c compares wrappers by this pointer (sb.c:225); input chunks hold it as void *chunk (flb_input_chunk.h:96).
identities.owner: Storage ownership: the cio stream lists inside config->cio (ch->_head / ch->_state_head, cio_chunk.h:44-50), created by flb_storage_create (flb_storage.c:713-736) and destroyed by cio_destroy (flb_storage.c:1000). unresolved_summary.missing_premise: completion identity: key is (ret, task id, output id) without generation; engine lookup config->task_map[id] has no NULL/generation check (src/flb_engine.c:601-606). Needs a stated invariant that an outstanding user pins the slot, or a generation.

engine->worker task handoff is ordered only by the pipe write/read (src/flb_output_thread.c:450, 290); engine-side writes to shared task state (task->event_chunk at src/flb_engine_dispatch.c:155, chunk up/lock/down at src/flb_input_chunk.c:3796-3809 and src/flb_task.c:371-381, route removal in test mode at src/flb_engine_dispatch.c:267-268) have no lock against a worker concurrently serving another route of the same task; task->lock covers only route data (include/fluent-bit/flb_output.h:768-783, 1315-1324).

task->users is a plain int (include/fluent-bit/flb_task.h:90, 179-194); all selected mutations are on the engine thread, but reads in src/flb_input_chunk.c:706, 870, 911, 3178 run on the caller thread of chunk append, which is not established for flb_input_chunk_append_raw_local callers (outside_selection: src/flb_input_log.c).
eviction (sb_release_output_queue_space, task destroy with pending retries) is on the engine thread only if every chunk-append entry is; not established for the outside_selection caller above.
ownership of the chunk after a NULL flb_input_chunk_map return depends on the callee arm (src/flb_input_chunk.c:1512-1516 closes; others do not) and is not conveyed to cb_queue_chunks.

shutdown re-segregation (src/flb_engine.c:1510-1515): which chunks exist in the shared cio context at grace_count==1, whether they are already wrapped or owned by an ic, and whether the storage_backlog collector is paused (flb_input_pause_all, outside_selection).
backlog teardown runs after output instances are freed (src/flb_engine.c:1648 before 1650) and does not reach the unlinked queue's own wrappers; no source-level ordering keeps backlog->ins alive.
worker exit is ordered by pthread_join only when the stop write succeeds (src/flb_output_thread.c:632-640); the failure arm frees th_ins without join.

route->retry_context_destroy (src/flb_task.c:914-917) runs after the owning output plugin's cb_exit (src/flb_output.c:590-592); completions still queued in ins->ch_events at shutdown are never processed, so teardown relies on destroying tasks regardless of users (src/flb_engine.c:125-139).

whether downing or re-locking a task's chunk for a retry (src/flb_task.c:371-381, src/flb_engine_dispatch.c:98-118) can overlap a worker reading the previously mapped buffer for another route; only the users<=1 guard is visible.
